input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds the Customer (Meridian) with a post-term non-compete of twenty-four months, covering "any product or service that competes with Vendor" in "any territory", with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (indeed it expressly bars acquisitions). That is walk-away territory on two counts: post-term duration exceeding 12 months and effectively undefined scope. It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no non-compete commitment. Preferred position is no restriction at all, so we delete § 12.4 and leave § 12.3 to govern; the narrowed fallback (single named product, term only, with carve-outs) is offered in the comment if Vendor needs some protection.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept any restriction on the businesses we operate or the products we develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted § 12.4; a 24-month, all-product, worldwide post-term non-compete is outside our playbook and directly contradicts § 12.3. If Vendor needs protection for a specific offering, we could discuss a restriction limited to one named competing product during the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
